title: Respiratory Therapy Daily Note - Ventilator Day 2
author: D. Alvarez, RRT
summary: Ventilator day 2 on AC/VC FiO2 0.40/PEEP 5, SAT done at 08:00, not yet ready for SBT during resuscitation; VAP bundle and inhalation-injury nebulizer protocol continued.
body:
**Reason for Note**
Daily ventilator management, ICU day 2. Flame burn 22% TBSA with grade 2 inhalation injury (bronchoscopy 04:20 Mon). Intubated 02:50 Mon in the ED.

**Events / Subjective**
- SAT performed 08:00 with J. Morales, RN: propofol held (was 30 mcg/kg/min), fentanyl continued at 100 mcg/h. Patient woke to voice, followed commands with the left hand, was tearful, coughed forcefully on the ETT. No ventilator dyssynchrony or biting. During SAT HR 92, BP 110/65 (MAP 80), RR 17, SpO2 98%.
- Propofol restarted 08:35 at 20 mcg/kg/min for tearfulness and ongoing resuscitation per burn team.
- Current RASS -2, CPOT 1/8.

**Ventilator Settings (08:00)**
- Mode AC/VC, VT 450 mL (6 mL/kg IBW 75 kg), set RR 16, total RR 17, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.40 (weaned from 0.50 at 04:00).
- PIP 24, Pplat 17 cmH2O, driving pressure 12, static compliance about 38 mL/cmH2O.
- ETT 8.0 oral, 24 cm at the teeth, cuff pressure 24 cmH2O (goal 20-30), re-checked this shift. Ties and bite block intact, no skin breakdown at the lips.

**ABG (06:00, FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5)**
pH 7.41 / PaCO2 40 / PaO2 124 / HCO3 25 / BE +1, SaO2 98%, lactate 1.4. P/F ratio 310. Last COHb 3.0% (Mon 12:00), resolved. Pulse oximetry now reliable.

**Secretions / Breath Sounds**
Moderate thin white-tan secretions via in-line suction, suctioned 3 times since 04:00. Carbonaceous flecks markedly less than Monday. Breath sounds coarse bilaterally with scattered rhonchi that clear with suctioning; no wheeze. No bronchoscopy needed today.

**Nebulized Inhalation Injury Protocol**
Albuterol 2.5 mg q4h (last 08:00), acetylcysteine 20% 3 mL q8h (last 03:00, next 11:00), heparin 5,000 units nebulized q8h (last 07:00). Given in-line, albuterol first, then acetylcysteine, then heparin, with suction after. No bronchospasm, no tachycardia response. Continue per protocol.

**Weaning Assessment**
Not ready for SBT today. Reasons: still in the resuscitation phase (Parkland window ended 01:30; albumin 5% 500 mL running 06:00-10:00 with LR 75 mL/h), airway and facial edema with fluid shifts, FiO2 0.50-0.40 with PEEP 5 only since Monday afternoon, 14:00 dressing change requires sedation, no cuff leak test yet. Plan to reassess for SAT/SBT pairing Wednesday morning.

**VAP Bundle**
- HOB 30-35 degrees confirmed; oral care with chlorhexidine 0.12% q12h (next 09:00) plus oral suction q4h and PRN
- Daily SAT done; SBT screen done (fails readiness)
- Pantoprazole and SQ heparin on MAR
- Closed in-line suction, circuit not changed unless soiled; subglottic suction ETT not available
- Cuff pressure checks q shift

**Plan**
1. Continue AC/VC 450 x 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.40, titrate FiO2 for SpO2 92% or higher.
2. Continue nebulizer protocol; suction PRN.
3. ABG with next scheduled draw and with any ventilator or clinical change.
4. Daily CXR 05:00 reviewed with team.
5. Will reassess SBT candidacy tomorrow 08:00 with RN, MD.

D. Alvarez, RRT, Respiratory Therapy, filed 08:45.

title: Nutrition Follow-Up Note
author: P. Moreno, RD
summary: Tube feeds at goal 70 mL/h since 06:00; low prealbumin and phosphorus 2.1 (refeeding/burn losses); propofol calories counted; recommends protein modular and electrolyte repletion.
body:
**Reason for Follow-Up**
Hypermetabolic burn patient (22% TBSA, about 8% full-thickness, inhalation injury), mechanically ventilated, enteral nutrition day 2. Admission weight 82 kg, height 180 cm, IBW 75 kg. Bed-scale weight not reliable with edema and arm elevation.

**Nutrition Support**
- Osmolite 1.5 via OG tube started Mon 10:00 at 20 mL/h, advanced by 10 mL/h q4h, reached goal 70 mL/h at 06:00 today. Tolerating: abdomen soft, no emesis, gastric residuals below 100 mL per RN, no loose stool. Bladder pressures 10-14 mmHg during resuscitation.
- Goal regimen delivers about 1,680 mL/day = 2,520 kcal and 105 g protein, plus free water flushes 30 mL q4h.
- Estimated needs: about 2,450 kcal/day (Toronto-type estimate; Curreri about 2,930 and likely overestimates), protein 1.5-2 g/kg = 125-165 g/day. Indirect calorimetry not available.
- Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min (14.8 mL/h of 10 mg/mL) provides about 390 kcal/day from lipid, so total delivered is about 2,900 kcal/day. Slightly above estimated needs, accepted while sedated; will reduce EN if propofol continues at higher rates or if glucose/triglycerides rise.

**Pertinent Labs**
- Prealbumin 7.1 mg/dL (low; acute-phase suppressed, trend only), albumin 2.6 g/dL
- Triglycerides 168 mg/dL at 06:00 on propofol (mildly high, acceptable; recheck Thursday)
- Phosphorus 2.1 mg/dL (3.4 on admission), Mg 1.6 mg/dL (low), K 3.9, Na 134, Ca 7.7, BUN 23, creatinine 1.1
- Glucose 177 at 06:00; POC glucose 169-179 mg/dL this morning on insulin infusion 1.5 units/h (started 00:30). Latest 173 at 10:30.
- AST 72, ALT 58 (mild, stress/burn related)

**Assessment**
Severe burn hypermetabolism with early protein-calorie deficit risk. Falling phosphorus and magnesium after feeding advancement and fluid shifts indicate refeeding physiology plus burn and resuscitation losses. High risk for hyperglycemia from stress response and overfeeding. Protein delivery of 105 g is below the 1.5-2 g/kg range needed for wound healing.

**Recommendations**
1. Continue Osmolite 1.5 at 70 mL/h; do NOT hold for dressing changes (hold only for OR or extubation).
2. Add protein modular 15 g BID via OG (30 g/day) to reach about 135 g protein/day.
3. Replete phosphorus, magnesium and potassium per MD protocol; recheck BMP/Mg/Phos q6h until phosphorus is 2.5 or higher.
4. Continue thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, multivitamin with minerals, vitamin C 500 mg BID, zinc sulfate 220 mg daily (wound healing).
5. Continue insulin infusion for goal glucose 140-180 mg/dL; reassess EN total if insulin requirement climbs.
6. Calorie and protein adjustment needed when propofol is weaned: EN becomes the sole source.
7. Weekly weights when feasible; prealbumin and CRP weekly; consider 24-hour urine urea nitrogen Thursday.

P. Moreno, RD, will follow daily.

title: Wound Care Specialist Note - New Concerning Findings
author: N. Ibarra, RN (Burn Nurse Specialist)
summary: At the 14:00 dressing change the right chest and arm wounds showed new purulent drainage, foul odor, spreading erythema and a dark violaceous area at the right chest border; margin marked and burn surgeon notified.
body:
**Reason for Visit**
Daily burn dressing change at 14:00 with J. Morales, RN. Premedicated with hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV at 13:45. Gown, gloves, mask, sterile technique.

**Pre-Procedure Status**
HR 105, BP 106/55 (MAP 72), RR 20, SpO2 98% on vent (FiO2 0.40), Tbladder 100.4 F (99.9 F at 13:00, 99.5 F at 09:00). CPOT rose to 5/8 with dressing removal (1/8 at rest), propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. UOP 41 mL/h at 13:00-14:00.

**Findings**
- Right anterior chest (deep partial with full-thickness patches): new thick yellow-green purulent drainage on the inner dressings, foul odor noted on removal (was none Monday). Eschar beginning to separate at the lateral/inferior border, with a dark violaceous, non-blanching area about 4 x 5 cm at the right chest border and loss of the adjacent eschar adherence.
- Erythema spreading beyond the burn margin, about 2-3 cm in the lateral chest wall and toward the axilla, warm, indurated. Margin traced with skin marker at 14:30 and dated/timed on the skin.
- Right upper arm (deep partial): moist, increased exudate, no frank pus; forearm and hand (full-thickness) with escharotomy incisions open, clean, no purulence. Doppler signals present at radial and ulnar arteries of the right hand, capillary refill sluggish but present at fingertips, no tense compartments.
- Face/neck: superficial areas clean, dry, bacitracin applied, no concern.
- Pain response increased on chest assessment (grimacing, guarding), CPOT 5.

**Care Provided**
Wound cleansed with warm saline and chlorhexidine-free wound cleanser, loose debris removed, no sharp debridement performed. Photographs (6) taken with measurement ruler and uploaded to the media tab. Silver sulfadiazine 1% reapplied per the current order pending surgeon review, covered with dry sterile dressings, arm elevated and splint reapplied. Patient tolerated with transient HR rise to 108 and CPOT back to 4 by 15:00.

**Culture Plan**
Wound swab from the area of purulent drainage after cleansing, plus recommend blood cultures x2, tracheal aspirate, urine culture and lactate/procalcitonin (sepsis order set) given fever trend, tachycardia and fall in UOP. Cultures to be drawn before any antimicrobial. Biopsy for quantitative culture and histology per surgeon.

**Notifications**
- J. Morales, RN notified at bedside and agrees to escalate on SBAR.
- Dr. Okafor (Burn Surgery) paged 14:40, returned call 14:45; will examine at the bedside this afternoon and decide on topical agent change and biopsy. Will update Dr. Brandt.

**Recommendations**
1. Surgeon bedside exam today; consider switch to mafenide acetate (eschar penetration).
2. Monitor temperature, HR, MAP, UOP and glucose q1h; watch for sepsis.
3. Recheck the marked margin q4h and with each shift, document change in mm.
4. Maintain contact precautions and dedicated equipment.

N. Ibarra, RN, Burn Nurse Specialist, will return for the next dressing change.

title: Burn Surgery Event Note - Early Invasive Burn Wound Infection
author: R. Okafor, MD
summary: Bedside wound exam 16:30 consistent with early invasive burn wound infection; biopsy sent, silver sulfadiazine stopped, mafenide soaks starting 17:30, broad antibiotics given.
body:
**Reason for Note**
Event note: concern for burn wound infection raised by N. Ibarra, RN at 14:00 dressing change, and by RN SBAR at 15:30 for fever, tachycardia and falling urine output.

**Interval History**
Post-burn day 2. Resuscitation phase complete (Parkland 24 h ended 01:30). Since about 13:00 temperature has risen from 99.9 F to 101.4 F (16:30), HR 97 to 116, RR 26, MAP 67. UOP 28 mL/h at 15:00-16:00 (0.34 mL/kg/h) on LR 100 mL/h. CPOT 5 with dressing change, now 2.

**Exam (bedside 16:30)**
- Vitals 16:30: HR 116, BP 105/48 (67), RR 26, SpO2 96%, T 101.4 F. Ventilated, RASS -2.
- Right anterior chest: purulent drainage and foul odor, eschar separating along the lateral/inferior border with a dark violaceous area about 4 x 5 cm, surrounding erythema 2-3 cm beyond the burn margin, at the 14:30 marker line and extending slightly past it superolaterally. Tissue under separating eschar is soft, dusky, no bleeding on probing.
- Right upper arm deep partial: increased exudate, no purulence. Right forearm and hand full thickness: escharotomy sites clean, Doppler signals intact.
- Face and neck: no change.

**Data**
Lactate 2.9, WBC 18.4 (12.8 on admission, 15.4 at noon), Hgb 11.6, platelets 171, INR 1.4, aPTT 38, procalcitonin 4.8 (15:55). Creatinine 1.1 at noon. Cultures sent 15:50: blood x2 (peripheral and central), wound, tracheal aspirate, urine.

**Procedure**
Punch biopsy of the wound-margin tissue from the right chest border (viable/nonviable interface) obtained 16:35 after local lidocaine with existing sedation/analgesia; hemostasis with pressure. Specimens to microbiology for quantitative culture and to pathology for histology (looking for organism invasion of viable tissue). No complications.

**Assessment**
Early invasive burn wound infection of the right chest (and possibly arm) with systemic inflammatory response, likely evolving burn wound sepsis. Gram-positive organism (S. aureus) most likely at day 2, but Gram-negatives including Pseudomonas must be covered until cultures return. Evidence of hypoperfusion (lactate rising, oliguria).

**Plan**
1. Stop silver sulfadiazine (discontinued 16:45). Start mafenide acetate 5% solution soaks to right chest and right arm at 17:30, then q8h; keep gauze moist. Monitor for metabolic acidosis (BMP, ABG) and pain with application; premedicate.
2. Antibiotics: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV extended infusion started 16:30; vancomycin load 1,750 mg started 16:45; pharmacy dosing. Narrow when cultures and biopsy return.
3. Sepsis bundle with Dr. Brandt: fluid bolus, repeat lactate, vasopressor if MAP under 65; ICU team managing.
4. Re-mark erythema margin q4h; photos daily.
5. Early excision and autografting of right chest, forearm and hand once hemodynamically stable and infection controlled; tentatively Friday 11-06; will discuss consent with family. Type and screen current.
6. Continue hourly neurovascular checks right hand, elevation, splint.
7. Will re-examine in the morning and sooner for hemodynamic change.

R. Okafor, MD, Burn Surgery, filed 16:45.

title: Critical Care Event Note - Sepsis / Septic Shock
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: Burn wound sepsis progressing to vasopressor-requiring shock; cultures sent, pip-tazo and vancomycin given, two LR boluses, norepinephrine started 17:30; ventilator and steroid plans.
body:
**Reason for Note**
Event note, sepsis / septic shock in setting of early invasive right chest/arm burn wound infection, called by RN and burn team.

**Timeline Since 13:00**
- 13:00: T 99.9 F, HR 97, MAP 77, UOP 45 mL/h
- 14:00: T 100.4 F, HR 105, MAP 72; wound change shows purulence (see Wound Care and Burn Surgery notes)
- 15:30: T 101.1 F, HR 113, RR 23, MAP 69; RN SBAR to Dr. Okafor and me
- 15:50-15:55: cultures (blood x2, wound, tracheal aspirate, urine) and labs: lactate 2.9, WBC 18.4, platelets 171, INR 1.4, procalcitonin 4.8
- 16:30: T 101.4 F, HR 116, RR 26, MAP 67; piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g extended infusion started
- 16:45: vancomycin 1,750 mg load (20 mg/kg) started over 2 h
- 17:00: lactate 3.8; T 101.6 F, HR 122, RR 27, MAP 66; LR 500 mL bolus started
- 17:15: BP 101/44, MAP 63 despite bolus
- 17:30: norepinephrine started 0.05 mcg/kg/min via left IJ central line; MAP 64
- 17:45: second LR 500 mL bolus

**Current Status (about 17:50)**
HR 121, BP 102/45 (MAP 64) rising on norepinephrine 0.05, RR 27, SpO2 95% on FiO2 0.40, T 101.7 F. UOP 28 mL/h (15:00-16:00) then 24 mL/h (16:00-17:00), 0.3 mL/kg/h. RASS -2 on propofol 30, fentanyl 100; PIP up to 28 and Pplat 21 (from 24/17 this morning). SpO2 down from 98% at 14:00. Extremities warm, brisk cap refill, abdomen soft, bladder pressure last 12 mmHg at noon.

**Data**
Lactate 2.9 then 3.8. K 3.8, Mg 1.9, phosphorus 2.6 (after replacement), creatinine 1.1, glucose 226 (insulin infusion at 1.5 units/h). INR 1.4, aPTT 38, fibrinogen 380: no overt DIC, will trend. Hgb 11.6.

**Assessment**
Septic shock from burn wound infection (right chest/arm), with hypoperfusion (lactate 3.8, oliguria) and ongoing hypotension after 1 L crystalloid. SIRS criteria are unreliable in burn patients (baseline hypermetabolism, tachycardia, low-grade fever), but this trend is unmistakable: temperature above 101 F, HR above 120, RR above 26, new oliguria, rising lactate and falling MAP. Early hypoxemia and rising airway pressures suggest capillary leak/early ARDS physiology. Patient is already about 12% above Parkland, so further large boluses carry risk.

**Plan**
1. Hemodynamics: goal MAP 65 or higher. Titrate norepinephrine by 0.02-0.04 mcg/kg/min q5-10 min; vasopressin if above 0.25. Limit further crystalloid; albumin 5% 500 mL overnight. Repeat lactate at 19:00, goal clearance at least 10-20% q2h.
2. Antimicrobials: pip-tazo q8h and vancomycin per pharmacy AUC dosing. Cultures pending. Narrow at 48 h or with results.
3. Stress-dose hydrocortisone 50 mg IV q6h if norepinephrine requirement continues to rise.
4. Glucose: increase insulin infusion per protocol to goal 140-180.
5. Ventilator: at 18:00 raise PEEP to 8, FiO2 0.50, set RR 18 (total RR 27-28, early ARDS lung protection, keep VT 450, Pplat below 30). ABG 30-45 min after changes; portable CXR now. Increase sedation (propofol, fentanyl) for dyssynchrony.
6. Goals: MAP at least 65, UOP at least 0.5 mL/kg/h (41 mL/h), lactate downtrending, SpO2 92% or higher. Daily SAT deferred while in shock.
7. Continue heparin SQ prophylaxis (platelets monitored), pantoprazole.
8. Family (Jenna Whitaker, Linda Delaney) updated by Dr. Okafor. Full code.

Critical care time 55 minutes, excluding procedures.
L. Brandt, MD, Critical Care.

title: Portable Chest X-Ray, Single View
author: Radiology Service, Diagnostic Radiology
impression: Mild bilateral perihilar/interstitial opacities, no focal consolidation. ETT, OG tube and left IJ central line well positioned. Findings consistent with capillary leak / early ARDS physiology versus pulmonary edema.
summary: Mild bilateral perihilar interstitial opacities without consolidation; support devices well positioned.
body:
**Study**
Portable chest radiograph, single AP view, obtained 18:40.

**Clinical Indication**
Sepsis from burn wound infection, increasing oxygen requirement and airway pressures, ventilator changes (PEEP 8, FiO2 0.50).

**Comparison**
Chest radiograph 11/03/2026 05:00.

**Findings**
- Lines/tubes: Oral endotracheal tube tip approximately 4 cm above the carina. Orogastric tube with side port and tip below the diaphragm in the stomach. Left internal jugular central venous catheter tip at the cavo-atrial junction. ECG leads and monitoring wires overlie the chest.
- Lungs: New mild bilateral perihilar and interstitial opacities, symmetric, without dense focal consolidation or air bronchograms. No lobar collapse. Mild atelectasis at the right lung base unchanged.
- Pleura: No pneumothorax. No definite pleural effusion.
- Heart/mediastinum: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits for AP technique. No mediastinal widening.
- Bones/soft tissues: Right chest wall soft-tissue dressing material. No fracture or subcutaneous emphysema.

**Impression**
1. Mild bilateral perihilar/interstitial opacities, new since the prior study, no focal consolidation. Consistent with capillary leak / early ARDS physiology versus interstitial edema; clinical correlation advised.
2. ETT, OG tube and left IJ central line are well positioned.
3. No pneumothorax.

title: Pharmacy Antimicrobial and Vancomycin Dosing Note
author: A. Chen, PharmD
summary: Vancomycin 1,750 mg load given, AUC-guided plan with level before second dose; pip-tazo extended infusion, compatibility and renal monitoring; supports hydrocortisone for pressor-dependent shock.
body:
**Reason for Consult**
Antimicrobial dosing and monitoring, sepsis from early invasive right chest/arm burn wound infection (Dr. Okafor, Dr. Brandt). Weight 82 kg (dosing weight), height 180 cm, IBW 75 kg. No known drug allergies.

**Pertinent Data**
- Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL (17:00), estimated CrCl about 110 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault, actual weight); BUN 27. Burn patients often have augmented clearance and a larger volume of distribution, but sepsis and hypoperfusion raise the risk of AKI (UOP 20-28 mL/h this evening).
- WBC 18.4, platelets 171, procalcitonin 4.8, lactate 3.8 (17:00), 4.1 (19:00).
- Cultures sent 15:50 before antibiotics: blood x2, wound, tracheal aspirate, urine.
- Vitals 19:30: T 102.4 F, HR 133, MAP 69 on norepinephrine 0.12 mcg/kg/min.

**Vancomycin**
- Loading dose 1,750 mg IV (20 mg/kg actual weight) given 16:45 over 2 hours.
- Plan: AUC/MIC-guided dosing (target AUC24 400-600) using Bayesian software. Anticipated maintenance 1,250 mg IV q12h, first dose due about 04:30, to be finalized from the level.
- Level: vancomycin level 15 minutes before the second dose (04:15) to estimate clearance; dose will be adjusted by pharmacy. No trough-only targeting.
- Renal monitoring: BMP q12h (creatinine today 1.1), strict UOP, avoid additional nephrotoxins (no NSAIDs, contrast, aminoglycosides). Combination of vancomycin plus pip-tazo is associated with a higher risk of AKI; will watch closely and reassess need for vancomycin when cultures return. If MSSA is identified, will recommend switching to a beta-lactam.

**Piperacillin-Tazobactam**
4.5 g IV q8h as extended infusion over 4 hours (first dose 16:30). Rationale: time-above-MIC pharmacodynamics, augmented clearance and expanded volume of distribution in burn and septic patients, and need for reliable Pseudomonas and Gram-negative coverage. Next doses 00:30 and 08:30. No renal adjustment at this time.

**Compatibility and Administration**
- Vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam are Y-site incompatible at higher concentrations. Do not run through the same lumen simultaneously; flush with saline between agents. Suggest pip-tazo extended infusion via the left AC PIV or a dedicated lumen and vancomycin via a separate central lumen.
- Norepinephrine on a dedicated central lumen; propofol is lipid and should not be mixed with other drugs; insulin infusion on its own line.

**Other Review**
- VTE prophylaxis: heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h appropriate (platelets 171; if platelets fall below 100 or drop more than 50%, assess HIT).
- Stress ulcer prophylaxis: pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily appropriate (ventilated, burn greater than 20% TBSA, INR 1.4, steroids anticipated).
- Hydrocortisone: recommend stress-dose hydrocortisone 50 mg IV q6h if norepinephrine requirement continues at 0.1 mcg/kg/min or higher beyond about 1-2 hours (current 0.12). Monitor glucose (insulin infusion), potassium and sodium; plan taper once off vasopressors.
- Acetaminophen 1 g IV q8h scheduled: check LFTs daily (AST 72, ALT 58 this morning); max 3 g/day recommended.

A. Chen, PharmD, will follow cultures and levels.

title: Critical Care Progress/Event Note
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: Responding to resuscitation: lactate 4.1 to 2.6, norepinephrine steady at 0.14, hydrocortisone started 20:30; overnight plan to wean pressor and ventilator.
body:
**Interval Events**
Burn wound septic shock. Since last note: norepinephrine titrated 0.05 to 0.14 mcg/kg/min by 20:30 for MAP at or near 65-70 and has been held at 0.14 since. Hydrocortisone 50 mg IV given 20:30 (q6h). Albumin 5% 500 mL started 22:00 (to 02:00). Propofol 40 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 150 mcg/h for ventilator synchrony and comfort. Mafenide soaks given 17:30.

**Vitals (23:00)**
T 101.4 F (peak 102.4 F at 19:30), HR 117 (peak 133), BP 111/55 (MAP 74), RR 26, SpO2 96% on FiO2 0.50/PEEP 8. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8.

**Perfusion / Renal**
Lactate 3.8 (17:00), 4.1 (19:00), now 2.6 (22:30). UOP 20 mL/h at 18:00-19:00 then 28 -> 35 -> 42 -> 46 mL/h (22:00-23:00), 0.56 mL/kg/h. Creatinine 1.3 (23:00, 1.1 at 17:00), BUN 29, K 4.0, Mg 1.9, phosphorus 2.7. Extremities warm, cap refill under 3 seconds.

**Respiratory**
ABG 22:30 on AC/VC 450 x 18, PEEP 8, FiO2 0.50: pH 7.35 / PaCO2 38 / PaO2 98 / HCO3 20 / BE -5, SaO2 95% (P/F 196). Earlier ABG 18:45: 7.31 / 36 / 92. PIP 29, Pplat 22, driving pressure 14. CXR 18:40: mild bilateral perihilar/interstitial opacities, no consolidation, lines well positioned. Moderate thick tan secretions, suctioned by RT.

**Infectious / Heme / Endocrine**
- Wound Gram stain 21:30: many WBC, moderate Gram-positive cocci in clusters, consistent with S. aureus; cultures pending. Biopsy pending.
- WBC 21.8 with 14% bands, Hgb 10.9, platelets 142 (171 at 15:55). INR 1.4 earlier; watch for consumptive coagulopathy, heparin SQ prophylaxis continued, HIT unlikely given timing.
- Glucose 257 at 22:30, 241 at 23:30 on insulin infusion 5 units/h (increased from 4 at 21:00), down-trending; goal 140-180.
- Hydrocortisone and sepsis causing hyperglycemia; hourly POC glucose.

**Assessment**
Septic shock from MSSA-suspected burn wound infection, improving after source control measures, antibiotics, 1 L LR and albumin: lactate falling, UOP recovering, MAP stable on norepinephrine 0.14. Moderate hypoxemia with early ARDS physiology on PEEP 8.

**Plan Overnight**
1. Continue norepinephrine, MAP goal 65 or higher; begin weaning by 0.02 mcg/kg/min q15-30 min once MAP 70 or higher and lactate under 2; no more boluses unless UOP under 20 mL/h with low MAP.
2. Albumin 5% to finish at 02:00; LR reduced to 75 mL/h at 02:00; avoid fluid overload.
3. Next pip-tazo 00:30; vancomycin level at 04:15 before second dose (pharmacy).
4. Hydrocortisone 50 mg q6h (next 02:30).
5. Repeat lactate 02:00, BMP/CBC/LFTs/coags/PCT with morning labs (04:00-05:00), ABG 04:00.
6. Ventilator: wean PEEP toward 5 and FiO2 toward 0.40 as ABG and SpO2 allow; keep VT 450, Pplat under 30.
7. No SAT tonight; plan SAT and SBT assessment in the morning.
8. Family updated by phone: Jenna Whitaker aware of improving trend.

L. Brandt, MD, Critical Care.

title: Critical Care Progress Note
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: Septic shock resolving: norepinephrine off 04:30, blood culture bottle positive for GPC in clusters at 02:40, creatinine peaked 1.4, procalcitonin 9.6; plan SAT then SBT this morning.
body:
**Overnight Events**
- Norepinephrine weaned from 0.14 (00:00 0.12, 02:00 0.08, 04:00 0.04) and OFF at 04:30, MAP 77. Hydrocortisone 50 mg IV q6h continues (doses 20:30, 02:30; next 08:30). Pip-tazo 00:30 given; vancomycin 1,250 mg given 04:30 after level.
- 02:40: Critical call from microbiology: blood culture set 2 (central line) bottle 1 of 4 positive at 10 hours, Gram-positive cocci in clusters. Peripheral set 1 and other bottles pending. ID consult placed. Wound Gram stain (21:30) also GPC in clusters.
- Albumin 5% 500 mL completed 02:00. LR reduced to 75 mL/h at 02:00.
- Vent: PEEP weaned 8 to 6 at 02:00 (set RR 16), FiO2 0.50; PEEP 5 and FiO2 0.40 at 06:00 per RT.

**Vitals (07:00)**
T 100.1 F (Tmax 102.4 F at 19:30), HR 98, BP 112/61 (MAP 78), RR 17, SpO2 98% on vent. CPOT 1/8, RASS -2 on propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. PIP 24, Pplat 17, FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5.

**I&O / Renal**
UOP 51-68 mL/h (0.6-0.8 mL/kg/h) from 23:00, with one hourly entry of 280 mL at 02:00-03:00 attributed to delayed bag emptying; roughly 700 mL for 23:00-07:00. Creatinine 1.3 (23:00), peak 1.4 at 05:00 (baseline 0.9-1.1), BUN 30. Mild AKI (KDIGO stage 1) in setting of shock, vancomycin and pip-tazo. K 4.1, phosphorus 2.7, Mg 1.9, CO2 22, anion gap 9.

**Labs**
WBC 19.2 (21.8 at 21:00), bands 9% (14%), Hgb 10.4, platelets 128 (142 at 21:00; HIT unlikely, timing under 5 days, sepsis likely). Lactate 1.8 (02:00), 1.5 (05:00). Procalcitonin 9.6 at 04:00 (4.8 at 15:55), peak expected. Vancomycin level 11.6 mcg/mL (04:15, pre-dose). Albumin 2.0, AST 96, ALT 84, T bili 1.3 (hepatic changes of sepsis), INR 1.3, fibrinogen 350. Glucose 175; insulin infusion 1.5 units/h.
ABG 04:00 on FiO2 0.50/PEEP 6: pH 7.38 / PaCO2 39 / PaO2 104 / HCO3 22.
CXR 05:15: improving bilateral perihilar/interstitial opacities, no consolidation, lines in good position.

**Exam**
Sedated, arousable to voice, follows commands. Lungs coarse, improved. Abdomen soft, tolerating Osmolite 1.5 at 70 mL/h. Right arm elevated, splinted, dressings with mafenide soaks, Doppler signals present. Left radial A-line, left IJ CVC (day 3) sites clean.

**Assessment**
1. Septic shock from MSSA-suspected burn wound infection (right chest/arm) with possible bacteremia: pressor-free 2.5 h, lactate normalized, improving. Blood culture positive 1/4 bottles (GPC clusters).
2. Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with inhalation injury, early ARDS physiology now resolving (P/F 208 at 04:00 on FiO2 0.50/PEEP 6; FiO2 0.40/PEEP 5 since 06:00). Meets SBT screen: FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5, no pressor, MAP stable, lactate normal.

**Plan**

2. Continue pip-tazo and vancomycin; ID consulted (Dr. Raman). Repeat blood cultures when organism identified; central line stays for now, decision per ID.
3. Hydrocortisone 50 mg q6h until stable, taper to 25 mg q6h this afternoon; off by Thursday.
4. Wean LR 75 to 50 mL/h at noon; no more crystalloid after 18:00 if taking diet. Daily weight. Trend BMP q12h.
5. Insulin infusion to correction scale transition once glucose stable under 150 off sedation.
6. Continue heparin SQ and pantoprazole IV.
7. Family: updated by phone; patient still full code.

L. Brandt, MD, Critical Care. Critical care time 45 min.

title: Burn Surgery Progress Note
author: R. Okafor, MD
summary: Wound exam improved on mafenide; erythema contained at marked margin; biopsy results pending; tentative OR Friday 11-06; continuing broad antibiotics.
body:
**Hospital Day 3 / Post-Burn Day 3**
Flame burn 22% TBSA (about 8% full-thickness) with grade 2 inhalation injury. Early invasive wound infection and septic shock on Tuesday, resolving.

**Interval**
Norepinephrine off 04:30. Afebrile trend: T 102.4 F at 19:30, 100.1 F at 07:00. HR 98, BP 112/61 (MAP 78), SpO2 98% on vent. Blood culture bottle positive overnight (GPC in clusters), wound Gram stain GPC in clusters. UOP 51-68 mL/h overnight. CPOT 1/8 on fentanyl 100 mcg/h.

**Wound Exam (07:15, dressings down)**
- Right anterior chest: purulent drainage markedly decreased, malodor much reduced. Eschar separation at the lateral/inferior border stable; the dusky violaceous area about 4 x 5 cm has demarcated, no further extension. Erythema now contained at, and receding slightly inside, the 14:30 skin marker line (no spread beyond marker, 0.5-1 cm blanching band inside). Wound bed beneath the separating eschar pink-white, no new necrosis.
- Right upper arm deep partial: moist, less exudate, no purulence.
- Right forearm/hand full-thickness: escharotomy incisions clean, granulating edges, hand warm, Doppler signals strong at radial and ulnar arteries, cap refill 2-3 seconds, no tense compartments.
- Face/neck: healing, bacitracin.

**Topicals**
Mafenide acetate 5% soaks since 17:30 Tuesday (doses 17:30, 01:30; next 09:30). Tolerated with hydromorphone premedication. Bicarbonate 22 mmol/L, anion gap 9, pH 7.38 on 04:00 ABG: no evidence of mafenide-related metabolic acidosis; will monitor BMP/ABG q12h while soaks continue.

**Data**
WBC 19.2, bands 9%, platelets 128, Hgb 10.4, procalcitonin 9.6, creatinine 1.4, lactate 1.5. Wound biopsy (16:35 Tuesday): quantitative culture and histology pending; preliminary histology expected later today, final culture 48-72 h. Wound swab culture pending (Gram stain GPC in clusters).

**Assessment**
Early invasive burn wound infection of right chest, responding clinically to source-directed topical therapy, systemic antibiotics and resuscitation; MSSA suspected. Remains a candidate for early excision and grafting.

**Plan**
1. Continue mafenide 5% soaks q8h to right chest and arm; bacitracin to face BID; re-mark erythema margin q4h; daily photographs.
2. Antibiotics: pip-tazo 4.5 g extended infusion q8h and vancomycin per pharmacy; ID consulted. Narrow when identification and susceptibilities return.
3. Tentative OR Friday 11-06 for tangential excision and autografting of the right forearm/hand and chest, contingent on afebrile hemodynamic stability and negative repeat cultures. Will obtain consent from patient (once extubated and alert) with Jenna Whitaker present; NPO after midnight Thursday; type and screen to be refreshed Thursday.
4. Continue elevation, splint, neurovascular checks q2h right hand.
5. SAT and SBT this morning per ICU; extubation would be welcome.
6. Nutrition: continue Osmolite 1.5 at goal with protein modular.
7. Pain: premedicate before dressing changes (hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV 15 min prior); avoid benzodiazepines.

title: Respiratory Therapy SBT / Extubation Readiness Note
author: D. Alvarez, RRT
summary: SAT passed at 08:00; SBT on PS 5/PEEP 5/FiO2 0.35 for 30 minutes passed with RSBI 58 and cuff leak present; ABG 09:00 acceptable; team notified.
body:
**Reason for Note**
Ventilator day 3, SAT/SBT pairing per daily protocol; patient meets readiness criteria after septic shock resolved (norepinephrine off 04:30).

**Readiness Screen (08:00)**
- FiO2 0.40 then 0.35 (reduced at 09:00), PEEP 5, SpO2 98%, MAP 76-77, no vasopressor, low-grade temperature 99.8 F at 08:00, HR 97, cough strong, secretions manageable, not receiving neuromuscular blockade.
- Pip-tazo/vancomycin on board, hydrocortisone 50 mg q6h.

**SAT (08:00)**
Propofol OFF at 08:00 (was 30 mcg/kg/min), fentanyl continued at 100 mcg/h. RASS 0, CPOT 0/8, calm, follows commands, no agitation, HR 97, BP 111/60 (MAP 77), RR 18, SpO2 98%. SAT passed.

**ABG 09:00 (AC/VC 450 x 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.35)**
pH 7.40 / PaCO2 40 / PaO2 96 / HCO3 24 / BE 0 / SaO2 97%; P/F 274.

**SBT (started 09:25, ordered for 09:30)**
- Settings: pressure support 5 / PEEP 5 / FiO2 0.35 for 30 minutes (completed 09:55).
- Parameters at 30 min: RR 18, exhaled VT about 310 mL, RSBI 58 (pass under 105), SpO2 97%, HR 94-96 (no more than 5% change), BP 110/60, no accessory muscle use, no diaphoresis, no distress, MIP -26 cmH2O.
- PIP before trial 23, Pplat 16 on AC.

**Cuff Leak**
Cuff deflated: audible leak present, measured leak about 190 mL (greater than 110 mL or greater than 10-12% of VT). Lower risk for post-extubation stridor, although airway edema from inhalation injury and 2 days of resuscitation remains a concern.

**Secretions**
Moderate thin white secretions, suctioned before the trial; no thick tan secretions now. Cough effective on command.

**Assessment**
Passed SAT and SBT: RSBI 58, RR 18, SpO2 97% on minimal support, cuff leak present, hemodynamically stable. Dr. Brandt informed at 09:55; agrees to extubate.

**Plan**
1. Extubation at about 10:45 after feeds off 10:30 and OG suctioned; Dr. Brandt, RN J. Morales and RT present.
2. Equipment at bedside: suction, bag-valve mask, reintubation kit (8.0 and 7.0 ETT, video laryngoscope), racemic epinephrine 2.25% neb ready for stridor.
3. Post-extubation: 4 L/min nasal cannula, incentive spirometer, HOB 45 degrees, ABG at 12:00, chest physiotherapy with cough assist as needed.
4. Inhalation injury nebulizer protocol complete with extubation (last doses: acetylcysteine 03:00, heparin 07:00, albuterol 08:00); RT to give PRN albuterol for wheeze.
5. NPO until bedside swallow screen.

D. Alvarez, RRT, Respiratory Therapy.

title: Extubation Procedure Note
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: Planned extubation at 10:45 to 4 L nasal cannula after passing SAT/SBT; hoarse voice without stridor; monitoring plan with racemic epinephrine available.
body:
**Procedure**
Planned extubation of 8.0 oral ETT (placed 02:50 Mon in the ED, 24 cm at the teeth, about 56 hours of mechanical ventilation).

**Indication**
Resolution of the acute process (septic shock off pressors since 04:30, inhalation injury grade 2 with improving oxygenation). Passed SAT at 08:00 and SBT (PS 5/PEEP 5/FiO2 0.35, RSBI 58, cuff leak present) with RT D. Alvarez.

**Pre-Procedure**
- Patient alert, RASS 0, follows commands, able to cough and lift head. HR 93, MAP 77, SpO2 99%, T 99.6 F.
- ABG 09:00 7.40 / 40 / 96 / 24. Hydrocortisone 50 mg given 08:30.
- Tube feeds stopped 10:30; OG tube to suction, stomach decompressed.
- Equipment for reintubation at bedside (video laryngoscope, bougie, 7.0 and 8.0 ETT, suction, BVM). Racemic epinephrine available. Patient and family (Jenna Whitaker at bedside) informed of the plan and risks.

**Procedure Description**
Time-out performed. Patient upright 45 degrees. Oropharynx and then ETT suctioned (small amount thin white secretions). Cuff deflated with audible leak. At 10:45, with a peak inspiratory effort, ETT removed in one smooth motion while suction was applied; the patient coughed immediately. Placed on 4 L/min nasal cannula. Left wrist restraint removed. Fentanyl infusion stopped at 10:45 (propofol was off since 08:00).

**Post-Extubation Assessment (10:50-11:00)**
- Vitals: 10:50 HR 95, BP 112/61 (MAP 78), RR 20, SpO2 97%, T 99.7 F; 11:00 HR 94, BP 112/63 (MAP 79), RR 22, SpO2 96% on 4 L NC.
- Voice hoarse but phonating clearly, weak cough, able to clear secretions. No stridor at rest, no accessory muscle use, no drooling. Breath sounds clear bilaterally with transmitted upper-airway sounds. Pain 4/10.
- Tolerated without desaturation or complications.

**Complications**
None. No blood loss.

**Plan**
1. Close monitoring: continuous SpO2 and cardiac monitoring, vitals and airway assessment q15 min for 1 hour, then hourly; RT at bedside.
2. For stridor or increased work of breathing: racemic epinephrine 0.5 mL of 2.25% in 3 mL NS neb, repeat q20 min x3, heliox if available, continue hydrocortisone, and call me immediately for reintubation readiness.
3. HOB 45 degrees or higher; incentive spirometry hourly, cough and deep breathing; voice rest.
4. NPO until bedside swallow screen (SLP to see); OG tube to be removed at 11:15. Aspiration precautions, oral care.
5. Dexmedetomidine 0.4 mcg/kg/h starting 11:00 for anxiety; CAM-ICU at noon. Avoid benzodiazepines.
6. ABG at 12:00. Dr. Okafor aware.
7. Wean oxygen to keep SpO2 92% or higher.

L. Brandt, MD, Critical Care.

title: Infectious Diseases Consultation
author: S. Raman, MD
summary: Positive blood culture bottle with GPC in clusters and wound Gram stain GPC in clusters in burn wound sepsis; MSSA likely; continue pip-tazo and vancomycin until identification and susceptibilities, repeat cultures, keep central line for now.
body:
**Reason for Consult**
Burn wound infection with positive blood culture (Gram-positive cocci in clusters). Requested by Dr. Okafor (Burn Surgery) and Dr. Brandt (Critical Care).

**History of Present Illness**
34-year-old man (82 kg) with house-fire flame burns 22% TBSA (about 8% full-thickness: right forearm/hand, anterior chest with deep partial areas) and grade 2 inhalation injury. Intubated 02:50 Monday, escharotomy right forearm 03:15, left IJ central line placed 03:45 Monday, left radial A-line 04:30 Monday. Silver sulfadiazine to wounds Monday and Tuesday. On Tuesday at 14:00 new purulent drainage, foul odor, erythema beyond the burn margin and a dusky area at the right chest border. T 101-102.4 F, HR to 133, MAP 63-64, lactate 2.9 to 4.1, norepinephrine 17:30 Tuesday to 04:30 Wednesday. Cultures drawn 15:50 Tuesday before antibiotics. Pip-tazo since 16:30 and vancomycin since 16:45 Tuesday. Extubated 10:45 today. PMH: childhood asthma (resolved), no meds, NKDA. Tdap given Monday. Smoker 15 pack-years, 4-6 beers weekends.

**Exam (11:00)**
T 99.5 F, HR 94, BP 112/63 (MAP 79), RR 22, SpO2 96% on 4 L NC. Hoarse, alert, answers appropriately. No murmur, no peripheral embolic stigmata (no Janeway lesions, splinters, Roth spots on gross exam). Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Left IJ central line site (day 3): clean, no erythema or purulence. Left radial arterial line site clean. Right chest: dressed with mafenide-soaked gauze; per Dr. Okafor's 07:15 exam drainage decreased and erythema within marker. Right arm splinted, hand warm.

**Data**
- WBC 19.2 (peak 21.8, bands 14% Tuesday 21:00 to 9% now), platelets 128, Hgb 10.4. Creatinine 1.4 (peak), BUN 30. Lactate 1.5. Procalcitonin 4.8 to 9.6 (04:00). AST 96, ALT 84, albumin 2.0.
- Vancomycin level 11.6 mcg/mL (04:15, pre-dose).
- Blood cultures x2 sets 15:50 Tuesday: set 2 (central line) bottle 1 of 4 positive at 10 hours (flagged 02:40 Wednesday), Gram-positive cocci in clusters; remaining bottles and set 1 (peripheral) pending. Final organism identification and susceptibilities pending at this time.
- Wound Gram stain (21:30 Tuesday): many WBC, moderate GPC in clusters. Wound swab and biopsy cultures pending. Tracheal aspirate and urine cultures pending.
- CXR 05:15: improving bilateral opacities without consolidation.

**Assessment**
1. Burn wound sepsis with early invasive infection, right chest/arm, and Gram-positive cocci in clusters bacteremia: most likely Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA likely given community onset, no prior hospitalization or antibiotic exposure; MRSA not excluded until susceptibilities). Differential: coagulase-negative staphylococci contaminant (less likely given heavy wound Gram stain and clinical sepsis). Source most likely the burn wound; line-related infection possible (central line day 3), but time-to-positivity of 10 hours in a single bottle, a clean insertion site and a wound with heavy GPC argue for wound source.
2. Septic shock, resolving.
3. Mild AKI (Cr 1.4) on vancomycin plus pip-tazo.

**Recommendations**
1. Continue piperacillin-tazobactam plus vancomycin until organism identification and susceptibilities return (expect within hours). If MSSA, narrow to cefazolin 2 g IV q8h (better than vancomycin); stop pip-tazo when wound cultures finalize without Gram-negatives. Pharmacy to dose vancomycin by AUC; avoid trough-only dosing.
2. Repeat blood cultures x2 (one peripheral, one from the central line) when the organism identification returns and before the next antibiotic dose; repeat q24-48h until clear.
3. Central line: retain for now since wound source is most likely and the patient needs central access; remove and replace at a new site if repeat blood cultures remain positive at 48-72 h, local site infection develops, or hemodynamic instability recurs. Daily necessity review.
4. Echocardiography not needed initially provided clearance within 72 hours, no murmur, no hardware; obtain TTE (and consider TEE) if repeat cultures stay positive, fever persists beyond 72 h, new murmur, or embolic signs.
5. Duration: if uncomplicated S. aureus bacteremia from a controlled source with documented clearance, at least 14 days of IV therapy counted from the first negative blood culture; longer (4-6 weeks) if complicated. Wound source control by excision and grafting Friday is essential.
6. Daily BMP, CBC, procalcitonin trend. Follow wound biopsy histology.
7. Standard and contact precautions. ID will follow daily and update as results return. Discussed with Dr. Okafor and Dr. Brandt.

S. Raman, MD, Infectious Diseases.

title: Nutrition Note - Post-Extubation
author: P. Moreno, RD
summary: OG removed 11:15 after extubation; swallow screen pending; plan oral soft high-protein diet with shakes, calorie counts, continue vitamin C and zinc.
body:
**Reason for Follow-Up**
Transition from enteral to oral nutrition after extubation. Burn 22% TBSA, hypermetabolic, nutrition day 3.

**Interval**
- Osmolite 1.5 via OG at goal 70 mL/h since 06:00 Tuesday; tube feeds stopped 10:30 today for extubation (10:45); OG tube removed 11:15. Feeds provided 2,520 kcal and 105 g protein/day plus protein modular; propofol off since 08:00 (no longer a lipid source).
- Currently NPO pending bedside swallow screen (SLP to evaluate). Voice hoarse after 56 h intubation, cough effective. On 4 L NC, SpO2 96%, RR 23.
- Alert, RASS 0, reports hunger and thirst, mild nausea after extubation, ondansetron 4 mg IV given 12:30. Abdomen soft, last stool Tuesday.
- Weight not rechecked; fluid-shifted. Admission weight 82 kg.

**Labs**
Albumin 2.0 g/dL, total protein 4.6, prealbumin 7.1 (Tuesday). Phosphorus 2.7 mg/dL, Mg 1.9, K 4.1, Na 137 (05:00); BUN 30, creatinine 1.4 (peak). POC glucose 150-154 mg/dL (10:30-11:30) on insulin 1 unit/h; infusion stopped at 12:00 and lispro correction scale started. AST 96, ALT 84, bilirubin 1.3, triglycerides 168 (Tuesday).

**Assessment**
Risk for inadequate oral intake: burn needs 2,450 kcal and 125-165 g protein/day, post-extubation dysphagia/odynophagia risk, anxiety, mafenide-associated pain with dressing changes, appetite suppressed by sepsis. A nutrition deficit is accumulating since feeds stopped at 10:30. Stress ulcer, refeeding and glucose control continue to matter.

**Recommendations**
1. Keep NPO until swallow screen passed; once cleared, advance to soft, high-protein, high-calorie diet (aspiration precautions per SLP), 3 meals plus snacks, with request for double protein portions.
2. Oral supplement shakes (high-calorie, high-protein, 350 kcal and 20 g protein each) three times daily with meals, plus a protein modular once daily in juice or shake. Goal oral intake 2,500 kcal and 130 g protein.
3. Calorie counts and protein tracking x72 hours; RN to document percent of meals eaten. If oral intake under 75% of goal after 48 hours, discuss placing a small-bore feeding tube for nocturnal supplemental feeds (needed especially before and after surgery Friday).
4. NPO after midnight Thursday for OR per surgery; plan to restart diet immediately after surgery; consider holding supplement only the minimum time.
5. Continue ascorbic acid 500 mg BID, zinc sulfate 220 mg daily, multivitamin with minerals, thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg to support wound healing (reassess after 10-14 days).
6. Glucose control per lispro scale; carbohydrate-consistent diet not required, but limit juices.
7. Replace phosphorus, Mg and K per protocol; BMP/Mg/Phos q12h.
8. Weekly weight; prealbumin and CRP weekly.

P. Moreno, RD, will follow daily and after the swallow screen.

title: Case Management Family Meeting Note
author: T. Whitfield, RN CM
summary: Family meeting at 13:30 with Ms. Whitaker, Ms. Delaney, Dr. Okafor and bedside RN: prognosis, OR plan, rehab, FMLA/short-term disability, transport and support for daughter.
body:
**Meeting**
Family meeting held at 13:30 in the Burn ICU family room (about 40 minutes). Present: Jenna Whitaker (partner and health care proxy), Linda Delaney (mother), R. Okafor, MD (Burn Surgery), J. Morales, RN (bedside), and T. Whitfield, RN CM. The patient (awake, hoarse, extubated at 10:45) was not present; Dr. Okafor updated him at the bedside afterward and he agrees with the plan.

**Medical Update (Dr. Okafor)**
- Marcus has flame burns to 22% of his body with inhalation injury. Tuesday he developed a serious infection in the burn wounds that spread to his blood and caused a drop in blood pressure; now stable, off the blood pressure medicine since 04:30, off the ventilator since 10:45. Cultures show a bacteria (germ identification pending); strong IV antibiotics running.
- Expected course: continued burn ICU care 1-2 more days, transfer to a burn step-down unit if stable. Burn surgery to remove dead tissue and place skin grafts tentatively Friday 11-06 (right forearm, hand and chest), likely a second procedure later. Grafts come from his own thigh; donor sites painful. Hospital stay likely 2-4 weeks.
- Prognosis: good for survival; function of the right hand depends on early therapy; scarring expected and long recovery with occupational therapy, wound care and pain management.

**Questions and Responses**
Ms. Whitaker asked about pain, how risky the surgery is, and when their daughter Ava (age 6) can visit; Ms. Delaney asked about long-term hand use and who will do the dressing changes at home. Dr. Okafor answered; consent for surgery to be completed with the patient on Thursday. Both are tearful but engaged and appreciative. Full code confirmed.

**Rehabilitation and Disposition**
Discussed two options: inpatient burn rehabilitation vs discharge home with outpatient burn clinic, home health nursing and outpatient OT/PT. Decision after surgery and PT/OT evaluation. Patient lives with his partner and daughter; their home was damaged by the fire, temporary housing needs assessed by K. Abara, LCSW (Red Cross referral in place).

**Financial / Work**
Patient is an HVAC technician. Ms. Whitaker given FMLA paperwork for caregiver leave and the patient's short-term disability forms for employer HR; I will fax forms with physician certification. Insurance authorization for the planned grafting submitted today (see CM notes).

**Family Support**
- Transport/lodging: Ms. Delaney's hospital-rate hotel referral; parking vouchers and shuttle passes provided to Ms. Whitaker and Ms. Delaney; meal vouchers.
- Child support: K. Abara arranging child life consult for Ava to prepare for a bedside visit (burn dressings, equipment) once he is stable and infection precautions allow with gown and gloves.
- Family encouraged to take breaks and rest; chaplain offered, declined for now.

**Plan**
1. Follow up after surgery with rehab vs home evaluation.
2. Submit FMLA/STD forms and track authorization.
3. Update family after each major change; CM contact number given.

T. Whitfield, RN CM.

title: Pharmacy Antimicrobial Stewardship Note - MSSA Identified
author: A. Chen, PharmD
summary: MSSA in 2 of 4 blood culture bottles and wound called 15:00; vancomycin stopped 15:30; recommends cefazolin 2 g q8h with pip-tazo continued as bridge until susceptibilities are final.
body:
**Reason for Note**
Antimicrobial stewardship review after microbiology called at 15:00: Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) in 2 of 4 blood culture bottles (one peripheral, one central line set drawn 15:50 Tuesday) and in the right chest/arm wound culture. Final susceptibilities pending. Discussed with Dr. Raman (ID) and Dr. Okafor.

**Current Antimicrobials**
- Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h extended infusion (started Tue 16:30; last dose 08:30, next due 16:30, then 00:30).
- Vancomycin: load 1,750 mg Tue 16:45, second dose 1,250 mg Wed 04:30 after pre-dose level 11.6 mcg/mL at 04:15. DISCONTINUED at 15:30 (MSSA, no MRSA). Next dose that would have been due about 16:30 is cancelled. Bayesian AUC estimate for the 24 h before the stop was in the target range (about 450); no further levels needed.

**Pertinent Data**
Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (05:00 peak, 1.1 Tuesday 17:00), BUN 30, UOP 69-72 mL/h (about 0.85 mL/kg/h) this afternoon. WBC 19.2, bands 9%, platelets 128, procalcitonin 9.6 (04:00); a repeat procalcitonin due 16:00. Afebrile trend T 99.4-99.6 F, HR 91, MAP 80, SpO2 96% on 4 L NC. Lactate 1.5. AST 96, ALT 84. Glucose 150-154.

**Assessment**
MSSA bacteremia, burn wound source most likely (heavy wound growth, GPC clusters on 21:30 Gram stain), septic shock resolved. Vancomycin is inferior to a beta-lactam for MSSA and adds nephrotoxicity when combined with pip-tazo, so stopping it is appropriate. Pip-tazo is a bridge for possible Gram-negative or polymicrobial burn wound flora until wound and biopsy cultures finalize.

**Recommendations**
1. Change to cefazolin 2 g IV q8h (dosing for 82 kg, CrCl about 100 mL/min; maximum 2 g per dose is sufficient for MSSA bacteremia). Recommended to ID; order expected from Dr. Raman after repeat blood cultures are drawn at 16:00. Start cefazolin with the first available scheduled slot once susceptibilities (cefazolin) are final, and stop pip-tazo then (anticipate by early Thursday).
2. Continue pip-tazo through the 16:30 and 00:30 doses until stewardship/ID signs off; no renal adjustment required.
3. Repeat blood cultures x2 at 16:00 before the next antibiotic dose; ID duration at least 14 days from first negative culture.
4. Renal: BMP q12h; creatinine 1.4 is expected to improve now that vancomycin is stopped. Avoid NSAIDs and IV contrast.
5. Vancomycin level: none needed; document the end of therapy.
6. Drug interactions/safety: mafenide soaks can cause metabolic acidosis through carbonic anhydrase inhibition (bicarbonate 22, anion gap 9): monitor BMP q12h, avoid additional carbonic anhydrase inhibitors. Hydrocortisone 25-50 mg raises glucose: lispro correction scale started noon. Gabapentin 300 mg TID (renal dose appropriate) plus oxycodone PRN and dexmedetomidine have additive sedation and respiratory depression; keep RASS 0, hold for RASS -2 or lower. Heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h continues; platelets 128 (nadir) with a low 4T score, HIT unlikely.
7. Hydrocortisone taper (50 mg q6h reduced to 25 mg q6h from the 14:30 dose) then stop; monitor BP and glucose.

A. Chen, PharmD, Clinical Pharmacy.

title: Physical Therapy Treatment Note - First Mobilization After Extubation
author: S. Kim, PT
summary: First OOB mobilization: supine to sit to chair with 2 assist, stable vitals, pain 4-6/10, right arm elevated and splinted; plan daily mobility.
body:
**Reason for Visit**
First mobilization after extubation (10:45) per OOB-to-chair order (12:00). Premedicated with hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV at 13:45. Burn 22% TBSA (right arm/chest), septic shock resolved. Present: S. Kim, PT, J. Morales, RN, and H. Larsen, OTR/L (co-treatment).

**Subjective**
Reports "I'm weak but I want to get up." Pain 6/10 at 14:00 before premedication, 4/10 at rest after. Hoarse voice, short sentences. Anxious about lines. Oriented, RASS 0.

**Pre-Mobility Status (14:00)**
HR 91, BP 114/63 (MAP 80), RR 20, SpO2 96% on 4 L/min NC, T 99.5 F. Lines/devices: left IJ CVC, left radial A-line, left AC PIV, Foley, tube feeds off; norepinephrine off, dexmedetomidine 0.4 mcg/kg/h infusing. Right arm in elevated splint.

**Intervention**
- Bed mobility: supine to sit at edge of bed with moderate assist x2, log-roll avoiding right chest and arm, HOB raised first. Right arm supported on pillow by OT.
- Dangle at edge of bed 5 minutes: HR 98, SpO2 95%, RR 22, mild dizziness that resolved with 2 minutes seated, no hypotension.
- Stand pivot to bedside chair with 2-person assist and gait belt, lines managed by RN. Tolerated standing 30 seconds (weak legs, trunk sway), pivoted to the chair at 14:30.
- Seated in chair about 30 minutes with legs elevated, performed left-sided active exercises, ankle pumps, heel slides, 10 reps x2, incentive spirometer 8 breaths x5 (about 1,000 mL).
- Returned to bed at 15:05 with 2 assist, tolerated well.

**Response / Post-Activity (15:00)**
HR 91, BP 112/64 (MAP 80), RR 21, SpO2 96% on 4 L NC, pain 4/10. Fatigue 5/10, no chest pain, no arrhythmia. Right hand warm, Doppler pulses unchanged per RN, edema stable.

**Assessment**
Deconditioning after 3 days of critical illness with sedation; strength 3+/5 lower extremities, 4/5 left upper extremity, right arm exercises limited to elevation. Needs moderate to maximal assist for transfers. Fall risk high. Good tolerance for first mobilization.

**Plan**
1. Mobilize twice daily with RN: chair 2-3 times for meals, then progress to marching in place and short ambulation with front-wheeled walker once standing tolerance improves.
2. Active range of motion of lower extremities and left arm; right shoulder and elbow ROM per burn protocol with OT.
3. Precautions: right arm elevated above heart, left IJ line and A-line precautions, fall precautions, assist x2, non-skid footwear, monitor SpO2 above 92%, HR below 130.
4. Premedicate 30-45 min before therapy. Avoid mobilization during dressing change window.
5. Continue pulmonary hygiene and IS hourly. Pre-op: encourage out-of-bed activity until Friday surgery, then post-graft restrictions per Dr. Okafor.

S. Kim, PT.

title: Occupational Therapy Treatment Note - Hand Therapy
author: H. Larsen, OTR/L
summary: OT session with PT for first chair mobilization; right arm edema control, splint wear and fit, active ROM left hand and right fingers as permitted.
body:
**Reason for Visit**
Burn rehabilitation: right hand and forearm full-thickness burn s/p forearm escharotomy, right upper arm deep partial, anterior chest. Co-treatment with S. Kim, PT for the first OOB transfer. Present: J. Morales, RN.

**Subjective**
Pain 4/10 at rest, 6/10 earlier today; premedicated hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV 13:45. Right-hand dominant (HVAC technician). Worried about losing hand function; reassured about the role of splinting and early ROM.

**Objective**
- Vitals before: HR 91, BP 114/63 (MAP 80), SpO2 96% on 4 L NC. After (15:00): HR 91, BP 112/64, SpO2 96%.
- Right arm elevated on pillows above heart level; moderate edema of hand and forearm, fingertips pink, cap refill 2-3 seconds, Doppler signals per RN present. Escharotomy incisions open and dressed in mafenide soaks; no new drainage or odor.
- Splint: resting hand splint in position of function (wrist 20-30 degrees extension, MCP 70-90 degrees flexion, IP joints extended, thumb abducted) fit intact, no pressure areas at ulnar border or thumb web after removal. Skin check done under the strap and padding, reapplied with Ace wrap.
- Active ROM left hand and wrist full. Right shoulder passive ROM to 90 degrees flexion, elbow 20-110 degrees, wrist limited by splint; gentle active finger flexion and extension in splint window, 5 repetitions x2, with tightness at PIPs.
- Self-care: needs maximal assist for ADLs; unable to feed self with right hand. Left-hand eating with built-up utensils trialed.

**Intervention**
1. Hand therapy: edema control (elevation, retrograde massage not applied over open wounds, active finger pumping), gentle active digit exercises hourly while awake with RN reminders.
2. Splint wear: splint on at all times except dressing change and therapy, check skin every shift; reapply after mafenide soaks. Written splint schedule posted at the bedside.
3. Positioning education: avoid shoulder adduction and elbow flexion contracture, axilla abduction 90 degrees on a pillow or arm trough when chest dressing allows.
4. Co-treated chair transfer with PT; sat in chair 30 minutes with arm trough.
5. Patient and Ms. Whitaker taught splint, elevation and exercise purpose; verbalized understanding.

**Assessment**
At high risk for hand contracture and scar; early ROM and splint wear essential. Good response to first session. Edema moderate. Surgery Friday (excision and graft) will require post-graft immobilization 5-7 days then ROM.

**Plan**
OT daily (twice daily post-op). Pre-op hand ROM and measurements recorded. Reassess splint fit after graft. Coordinate with PT and RN for premedication.

H. Larsen, OTR/L.

title: Speech-Language Pathology Bedside Swallow Evaluation
author: R. Imani, SLP
summary: Passed bedside swallow screen at 16:00 after 56 hours of intubation; voice hoarse; soft diet with thin liquids and aspiration precautions recommended.
body:
**Reason for Referral**
Post-extubation swallow evaluation (ETT 02:50 Mon to 10:45 Wed, about 56 hours). Inhalation injury grade 2, face and neck superficial burns, burn sepsis resolving. Nothing by mouth since extubation; OG tube removed 11:15.

**History / Subjective**
34-year-old man, alert, oriented x4, RASS 0. Reports sore throat and hoarseness, denies coughing with secretions or choking. Hungry and thirsty. No prior dysphagia. Dentition natural; no facial or oral burns in the oral cavity (perioral soot cleared).

**Objective**
- Vitals 16:00: HR 90, BP 112/64 (MAP 80), RR 20, SpO2 96% on 2 L NC (weaned from 4 L), T 99.3 F. Upright in bed 90 degrees.
- Oral mechanism: lips, tongue, palate symmetric; strength adequate; voice is hoarse and breathy with reduced volume (post-extubation laryngeal irritation), no stridor, no drooling. Volitional cough weak to moderate but effective; clears throat x1 on request.
- Trials at bedside: ice chips x3: no change. Thin water by teaspoon x6, then 3 oz (90 mL) water screen by cup, then puree (applesauce) x4 teaspoons, soft solid (soft cooked egg/crackers softened in pudding) x4. Oral phase timely, prompt swallow initiation with palpable laryngeal elevation, no cough, throat clearing, wet voice, or delayed cough at 1 minute. SpO2 stable 95-96% through trials.

**Assessment**
Passed bedside swallow screen at 16:00. Mild oropharyngeal weakness expected after prolonged intubation without clinical signs of aspiration. Dysphonia consistent with post-extubation laryngeal edema/irritation (hydrocortisone on board). Fatigue could change swallow safety later in the day.

**Recommendations**
1. Diet: soft (mechanical soft) solids with thin liquids; high-protein supplements per dietitian. Meds whole in puree if large.
2. Aspiration precautions: upright 90 degrees for meals and 30 minutes after, small bites and sips, slow rate, alternate solids and liquids, no straws initially, alert and supervised for the first meals, oral care before and after meals.
3. Stop feeding and notify RN/SLP for coughing, wet voice, new stridor, increasing work of breathing, SpO2 below 92%.
4. Voice conservation: limit talking, hydrate; if hoarseness persists beyond 5-7 days or stridor, request ENT laryngoscopy.
5. SLP to re-evaluate 24-48 hours after the first meals, and post-operatively if re-intubation or sedation.
6. Plan communicated to J. Morales, RN; diet order requested from Dr. Brandt.

R. Imani, SLP, Speech-Language Pathology.

title: ICU Transfer Summary
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: Complete 3-day Burn ICU summary for transfer to Med-Surg 2 East at 07:00: burn and inhalation injury, resuscitation, ventilation, burn wound sepsis with MSSA bacteremia, lines, antibiotics, pending items.
body:
**Patient**
Marcus Delaney, 34 M, MRN SIM-40101, 82 kg (admission), NKDA. Full Code. Contact precautions. Admitted Burn ICU 11/02 04:00; transfer to Med-Surg 2 East 11/05 07:00. Attending burn surgeon R. Okafor, MD; intensivist L. Brandt, MD; ID S. Raman, MD.

**Injury and ICU Course**
- House fire 01:30 11/02. Flame burns TBSA 22% (right arm circumferential 9%, forearm/hand full-thickness; anterior chest 9% deep partial with full-thickness patches; face/neck 4% superficial), about 8% full-thickness. Smoke inhalation: COHb 14.2% at 02:50 falling to 3.0% by 12:00 Mon; lactate 5.8 to 1.8 by Monday noon. Grade 2 inhalation injury on bronchoscopy 04:20 Mon. Cyanide treatment not required. Tdap given.
- ED: RSI intubation 02:50 (8.0 ETT), escharotomy right forearm/hand 03:15 with return of Doppler signal, left IJ central line 03:45, OG tube 03:05, Foley 02:45.
- Resuscitation: Parkland goal 7,216 mL LR in 24 h; actual crystalloid about 8,080 mL by 01:30 Tue (12% above goal; first 8 h about 3,965 mL vs goal 3,608), titrated to UOP 30-50 mL/h. Albumin 5% 500 mL x2 (Tue 06:00 and 22:00). Bladder pressures 10-14 mmHg; no abdominal compartment syndrome. LR stopped 18:00 Wed.

**Airway / Ventilation**
AC/VC VT 450 (6 mL/kg IBW), FiO2 1.0 weaned to 0.40 by Tue 04:00. PEEP 8/FiO2 0.50 Tue 18:00 to Wed 02:00 for sepsis-related early ARDS physiology (P/F nadir 184 at 18:45), improved by Wed 06:00. SAT/SBT passed Wed (RSBI 58, cuff leak present); extubated Wed 10:45 to 4 L NC; room air since 03:00 Thu, SpO2 95-97%. Hoarse voice, no stridor. CXR 05:20 Thu: clear, no infiltrate. Passed swallow screen Wed 16:00; soft diet.

**Infection / Sepsis**
Tue 14:00 new purulent right chest wound, erythema beyond margin, violaceous area. T to 102.4 F, HR 133, MAP 63, lactate peak 4.1 (19:00). Cultures 15:50, pip-tazo 16:30, vancomycin 16:45, LR 1 L, norepinephrine 17:30 (max 0.14 mcg/kg/min) off 04:30 Wed, hydrocortisone 50 mg q6h from 20:30 Tue then 25 mg from Wed afternoon, last dose 02:30 Thu. Wound biopsy 16:35 Tue. Silver sulfadiazine replaced by mafenide 5% soaks q8h from 17:30 Tue. Blood cultures: MSSA in 2 of 4 bottles (peripheral and central) called 15:00 Wed; wound culture MSSA. Vancomycin stopped 15:30 Wed. Pip-tazo last dose 00:30 Thu. Cefazolin 2 g IV q8h first dose due 06:10 Thu. Repeat blood cultures 16:00 Wed no growth to date. Procalcitonin 4.8 to peak 9.6 to 2.1 (Thu 04:30). WBC 21.8 peak, 11.2 now. Creatinine peak 1.4, now 1.0. Platelets nadir 128, now 186 (HIT unlikely).

**Vitals / Exam (05:00 Thu)**
T 98.8 F, HR 82, BP 112/64 (MAP 80), RR 18, SpO2 96% on room air. RASS 0, CAM-ICU negative Wed 12:00, pain 3/10 on oral regimen. UOP 52 mL/h (0.6 mL/kg/h). Lungs clear. Right arm splinted, Doppler present. Lab 04:30: Na 139, K 4.3, CO2 26, glucose 140, Cr 1.0, phos 3.1, albumin 2.0, AST 78, ALT 66.

**Lines and Devices**
- Left IJ triple-lumen CVC (placed 11/02 03:45, day 4): STAYS; ID says remove if repeat cultures positive. Chlorhexidine dressing, daily necessity review.
- Left radial arterial line and Foley removed 05:00 Thu. PIV left AC out Wed 18:00. OG out Wed 11:15, ETT out Wed 10:45. Needs a new PIV on arrival (NS 20 mL/h KVO via CVC).

**Medications of Note**
Cefazolin 2 g IV q8h; mafenide soaks q8h; bacitracin face BID; heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h; pantoprazole; acetaminophen/gabapentin/oxycodone PRN; vitamin C, zinc, MVI; lispro correction scale. Stopped: propofol (08:00 Wed), fentanyl (10:45 Wed), dexmedetomidine (03:00 Thu), norepinephrine, insulin infusion, hydrocortisone.

**Active Problems**
1. MSSA bacteremia / burn wound sepsis, resolving. 2. Burns 22% TBSA s/p resuscitation; OR Fri 11-06. 3. Inhalation injury, recovered airway. 4. Mild AKI resolved. 5. Stress hyperglycemia. 6. Nutrition/hypermetabolism. 7. Mobility/hand rehab.

**Pending / To Do on Med-Surg**
- Final blood culture susceptibilities; repeat blood cultures (final at 5 days); wound biopsy histology and quantitative culture.
- NPO after midnight Thu, consent for OR Friday, repeat type and screen this morning.
- Monitor fever, bicarbonate/chloride on mafenide, glucose, platelets.
- Calorie counts, supplements, PT/OT, ID follow-up, central line daily review, first void after Foley removal.
- Full code. Family: Jenna Whitaker (partner and proxy), Linda Delaney (mother); daughter Ava age 6; family updated and aware of transfer.

L. Brandt, MD, Critical Care.

title: Burn Surgery Transfer / Progress Note
author: R. Okafor, MD
summary: Post-burn day 3 summary; wounds improving on mafenide; transfer criteria met for Med-Surg; OR Friday for excision and autografting; recommendations to receiving team.
body:
**Summary**
Post-burn day 4 (injury 11/02 01:30), hospital day 4. 34 M, flame burns 22% TBSA (about 8% full-thickness) with grade 2 inhalation injury. Early invasive MSSA burn wound infection with bacteremia and septic shock Tuesday, resolved. Extubated Wed 10:45; norepinephrine off Wed 04:30.

**Overnight / Current**
T 98.8 F, HR 82, BP 112/64 (MAP 80), RR 18, SpO2 96% on room air. UOP 52-61 mL/h overnight (0.6-0.7 mL/kg/h). Pain 3/10 at rest on acetaminophen, gabapentin and oxycodone; dexmedetomidine off 03:00. Arterial line and Foley removed 05:00. Labs 04:30: WBC 11.2, Hgb 10.0, platelets 186, creatinine 1.0, CO2 26, procalcitonin 2.1.

**Wound Exam (05:30)**
- Right chest: no purulent drainage, no odor; erythema now clearly inside the 14:30 Tuesday marker line (about 1 cm receded). Violaceous area at the lateral border demarcated, eschar softened beneath mafenide, no new necrosis. Viable granulating margins.
- Right arm: upper arm partial thickness moist and pink, forearm and hand full-thickness eschar with escharotomy sites clean; Doppler signals strong, cap refill under 3 seconds, no tense compartments.
- Face/neck: healing, bacitracin.
- Wound culture final (06:00): heavy growth MSSA, susceptible to cefazolin, nafcillin, clindamycin, TMP-SMX; resistant to penicillin. Biopsy histology and quantitative culture pending.

**Antibiotics**
Pip-tazo last dose 00:30; cefazolin 2 g IV q8h first dose 06:10 (ID recommendation, matches susceptibilities). Mafenide acetate 5% soaks q8h to right chest and arm continue (next 09:30). BMP shows no acidosis.

**Assessment**
Burn wound infection controlled clinically; tolerating oral diet and analgesics; ready for excision and grafting Friday.

**Transfer Criteria (met)**
Off vasopressors more than 24 h (off since 04:30 Wed, about 25.5 h); extubated 19 h at this note and over 20 h by the 07:00 transfer; UOP adequate; MAP stable 76-82; pain controlled on PO regimen; room air since 03:00, SpO2 95-97%; afebrile below 100.4 F since Wed 05:00. Transfer to Med-Surg 2 East (burn step-down) at 07:00 approved with Dr. Brandt.

**Plan and Recommendations to Receiving Team**
1. OR Friday 11-06 for excision and autografting of right forearm/hand and chest (donor site thigh). NPO after midnight tonight (Thu to Fri); consent with patient and Jenna Whitaker Thursday; repeat type and screen this morning.
2. Wound care: mafenide soaks q8h (09:30, 17:30, 01:30), keep gauze moist; premedicate with oral oxycodone 30-45 min prior, hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV for severe pain; bacitracin to face BID. Daily photographs, mark erythema margin q shift.
3. Neurovascular checks right hand q2h (Doppler/cap refill), arm elevated, splint on except for care; call for loss of signal, pallor or tense forearm.
4. Vitals q4h; call for T 101.5 F or higher, HR over 120, MAP under 65, UOP under 30 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h) after Foley removal, new purulence or spreading erythema, bicarbonate under 18.
5. Labs: BMP, CBC daily; check blood glucose AC/HS.
6. Nutrition: soft diet, shakes TID, calorie counts. PT/OT daily.
7. ID follow-up; central line stays pending repeat cultures.
8. Family updated; Full Code.

R. Okafor, MD, Burn Surgery.

title: Pharmacy Transfer Medication Reconciliation
author: A. Chen, PharmD
summary: Transfer medication reconciliation for Med-Surg: active list with changes, cefazolin plan, medications stopped in the ICU, and monitoring.
body:
**Reason**
Medication reconciliation at ICU-to-Med-Surg transfer (07:00 Thu 11/05). 82 kg, NKDA. Creatinine 1.0 (04:30), CrCl about 120 mL/min. AST 78, ALT 66.

**Active Medications at Transfer**
- Cefazolin 2 g IV q8h (NEW): first dose given 06:10; next 14:10, 22:10. Planned at least 14 days from first negative blood culture, ID to set stop date. Wound culture final MSSA, cefazolin susceptible.
- Mafenide acetate 5% solution soaks to right chest/arm q8h (09:30, 17:30, 01:30). Monitor bicarbonate/chloride; pain on application.
- Bacitracin ointment to face BID.
- Heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h (06:00 given). Platelets 186.
- Pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily at 09:00; convert to 40 mg PO daily when eating well; continue for stress ulcer prophylaxis while burn greater than 20%.
- Acetaminophen: the 06:00 IV and 06:15 PO 1,000 mg doses are both documented (2 g in 15 min); this leaves 24-hour total at the 4 g limit. IV order discontinued; PO 1,000 mg q8h scheduled (next 14:00), maximum 3 g/day given mild transaminase elevation.
- Gabapentin 300 mg PO q8h (06:20 given).
- Oxycodone 5-10 mg PO q4h PRN pain (last 06:15); use 30-45 minutes before dressing changes.
- Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV PRN severe pain or dressing change if oral inadequate (last given 13:45 Wed).
- Insulin lispro correction scale AC/HS (infusion stopped 12:00 Wed); glucose 140-141.
- Senna-docusate 2 tablets BID (hold for loose stool), ondansetron 4 mg IV PRN nausea.
- Ascorbic acid 500 mg BID, zinc sulfate 220 mg daily, multivitamin with minerals daily, thiamine 100 mg and folic acid 1 mg daily.
- Oral supplement shakes TID (nutrition).

**Antimicrobial Plan**
Pip-tazo discontinued (last dose 00:30); vancomycin discontinued Wed 15:30 (last dose 1,250 mg 04:30 Wed, level 11.6 mcg/mL). Cefazolin alone for MSSA. Follow final blood culture susceptibilities and repeat cultures; consider oral step-down only per ID. Procalcitonin 2.1.

**Stopped in ICU (do not continue)**
Propofol (off Wed 08:00), fentanyl infusion (off Wed 10:45), dexmedetomidine (off Thu 03:00), norepinephrine (off Wed 04:30), hydrocortisone (50 mg q6h from 20:30 Tue, reduced to 25 mg q6h Wed 14:30; last dose 02:30 Thu, stopped 06:00), insulin infusion, lactated Ringer's (stopped Wed 18:00; NS 20 mL/h KVO), inhaled heparin/acetylcysteine/albuterol protocol, chlorhexidine oral rinse, lorazepam (avoid benzodiazepines).

**Starting / Needed on Med-Surg**
Cefazolin (above); PO analgesic regimen (acetaminophen, gabapentin, oxycodone); lispro correction scale; discontinue NS KVO if PIV/CVC not needed.

**Interactions / Monitoring**
- Gabapentin + oxycodone: additive sedation, keep RASS 0, hold for sedation; fall precautions; no benzodiazepines.
- Mafenide: carbonic anhydrase inhibition, check CO2/bicarbonate daily (CO2 26).
- Cefazolin: no significant interactions; watch diarrhea (C. difficile), rash.
- Heparin: platelets daily (186, HIT unlikely).
- Hydrocortisone stopped: monitor for hypotension, glucose trending down.

A. Chen, PharmD.

Prior authorization for excision and autografting (Friday 11-06) submitted Wednesday; awaiting payer decision (expedited review requested), clinical notes sent. Concurrent review for continued stay in progress. FMLA and short-term disability paperwork: forms received Wed; physician certification pending Dr. Okafor.

Family coping, tearful but engaged; K. Abara providing supportive counseling, child life referral for Ava. Patient anxious about surgery, improved with dexmedetomidine off and awake.

1. Hand off to 2 East case manager; I will follow post-operatively.

3. Discharge planning meeting after surgery.
